effort_breakdown.batch_write: ~3 hours — 800-1,000 items at 30/batch = 27-34 batches. Metadata-only: Difficulty→Easy, DifficultyScore→1, CognitiveLevel→Remember.
effort_breakdown.post_write_distribution_analysis: ~1 hour — re-compute Difficulty and Bloom's distributions, verify CAQS §6.1 targets now achievable.

tier_1_immediate.detection_methodology: Automated: tokenize stem text, tokenize correct-answer choice text, compute Jaccard similarity = |intersection| / |union|. If >50% overlap AND item has DifficultyScore ≥ 3 AND Bloom's level ≥ Understand → flag. Human review: verify the item genuinely tests recall (not application) before recalibrating. Batch verify 10% of flagged items to calibrate threshold.

tier_2_near_term.name: New Evaluate items — scenario-based professional judgment (Phase 1: 75 items)
tier_2_near_term.sections: A (ASC 842/740 judgment scenarios), D (make-or-buy, CVP decisions, pricing), E (ERM risk-response selection, control failure diagnosis), F (technology adoption recommendations)
tier_2_near_term.item_count_rationale: Phase 1 of 380. Target highest-impact sections first. Evaluate = professional judgment, recommendation, and decision-making under uncertainty. These are the hardest items to design — each requires: (1) a scenario with competing alternatives, (2) four plausible distractors each targeting a distinct judgment error, (3) explanation that teaches the decision framework, not just the answer. 75 items is 20% of the 380 total — Phase 1 proves the template before scaling.

per_section_allocation.A_asc_842_740_judgments: 15 items — Given a lease scenario with classification indicators, select the most appropriate accounting treatment. Given a deferred tax position with uncertainty, recommend the valuation allowance assessment.
per_section_allocation.D_cost_management_decisions: 20 items — Make-or-buy with qualitative factors (supplier reliability, capacity utilization, strategic fit). CVP scenario with multiple constraints (capacity, market, resource) — recommend optimal product mix.
per_section_allocation.E_erm_risk_response: 20 items — Given a risk assessment (likelihood × impact matrix), select the appropriate risk response (avoid/accept/reduce/share). Control failure diagnosis: given audit findings, recommend the most effective remedial control.
per_section_allocation.F_technology_adoption: 20 items — Given business requirements (cost, scalability, compliance, data sensitivity), recommend the appropriate technology (cloud vs. on-premise, RPA vs. full automation, specific analytics method).

effort_breakdown.template_design: ~3 hours — prototype 5 Evaluate items across sections, establish the 4-plausible-distractor pattern for judgment items. Test with single-item certification pass.
effort_breakdown.per_item_authoring: ~20 min/item average (75 items × 20 min = 25 hours). Higher than Apply items (10-15 min) due to distractor engineering complexity. Each distractor must represent a distinct, realistic judgment error.
effort_breakdown.per_item_review: Already included in authoring time — accounting review + psychometric review integrated per CAQS workflow
effort_breakdown.certification: ~2 hours (6-dimension verification per CAQS §1.6 across 75 items)

quality_requirements.distractor_engineering: Each Evaluate item needs 4 distractors that test different dimensions of judgment — not different calculation paths. Example targets: (D1) wrong decision framework applied, (D2) correct framework but wrong weighting of factors, (D3) ignores qualitative factors, (D4) selects technically correct but suboptimal recommendation.
quality_requirements.explanation_standard: Must teach the decision framework, not just state the answer. 'Why A is correct' = trace the full decision logic. 'Why B/C/D are wrong' = identify the specific judgment error in each.
quality_requirements.cognitive_authenticity: Items should feel like a controller presenting options to the CFO — not like a textbook asking 'which is correct?'

tier_2_near_term.success_metric: 75 Evaluate items in pool. All pass CAQS §1.6 six-dimension verification at HIGH confidence. Distractor quality: each distractor targets a distinct judgment error.

vdiff_item_characteristics.multi_step: ≥3 distinct calculation steps required before reaching the answer

risk_2_concurrent_write_data_loss.risk: Multiple Wave 1-2 operations write to the same pack files. DL-019 (concurrent-write data loss) can silently overwrite remediation.
risk_2_concurrent_write_data_loss.mitigation: Backup-before-write mandatory per BACKUP_PROTOCOL.md. Verify hash stability post-write. Exclusive session windows — no two agents writing to same pack file simultaneously. Write-lock protocol for all Tier 1-2 operations.

risk_3_evaluate_distractor_engineering.risk: EXP-006 Evaluate items require 4 distractors targeting distinct judgment errors. Template-based authoring cannot produce these — each distractor must be pedagogically engineered.

risk_3_evaluate_distractor_engineering.mitigation: Prototype 5 Evaluate items with expert review before scaling. Establish distractor design patterns (D1=wrong framework, D2=wrong weighting, D3=misses qualitative factor, D4=correct but suboptimal). Gate each batch through CAQS §1.6 at HIGH confidence.

risk_4_case_exhibit_validation_bottlenec.risk: EXP-009 requires per-case exhibit data-consistency verification. 60 cases × ~3 exhibits each = ~180 exhibits. Each exhibit must be internally consistent (subtotals → totals, section references correct, no decorative data).
risk_4_case_exhibit_validation_bottlenec.mitigation: Batch cases by file (scored_cases2 → 3 → 4 → 5). Reuse DL-023 exhibit normalization methodology. Automate row/column checks where possible.
